title: Detect SQL injection attempts
prompt: DEFENSIVE detection for a web firewall. Write `detect_sqli(value: str) -> bool` returning True if a request value looks like an SQL-injection attempt. Matching is case-insensitive. Flag it if it contains any of: a tautology like ' or 1=1 or ' or '1'='1 (a quote, then or, then number = same-looking number); `union select`; `drop table`; a semicolon then drop/delete/insert/update; a quote immediately followed by a comment -- or #; a /* */ comment; xp_cmdshell; or a time-delay call sleep(, benchmark(, pg_sleep( or `waitfor delay`. Otherwise return False. This only RECOGNISES attacks; it never builds them.
visible_tests: assert detect_sqli('normal search term') is False
hidden_tests: assert detect_sqli('1 UNION SELECT username, password FROM users') is True
assert detect_sqli("'; DROP TABLE users;") is True
assert detect_sqli('product WAITFOR DELAY 0:0:5') is True
assert detect_sqli('SELECT name FROM products WHERE id = 5') is False
assert detect_sqli('1 AND sleep(5)') is True

title: Detect cross-site scripting
prompt: DEFENSIVE detection. Write `detect_xss(value: str) -> bool` returning True if a value contains a cross-site-scripting payload (case-insensitive): an opening <script or closing </script> tag; a javascript: URI; an inline event handler onerror= onload= onclick= onmouseover= or onfocus= (optional spaces before =); a <svg or <iframe tag; or document.cookie. Otherwise False. Recognises only; does not generate payloads.
hidden_tests: assert detect_xss('') is True
assert detect_xss('I love javascript programming') is False

title: Detect path traversal
prompt: DEFENSIVE detection. Write `detect_path_traversal(value: str) -> bool` returning True if a value looks like a directory-traversal attempt (case-insensitive): it contains ../ or ..\\ ; a URL-encoded dot-dot (%2e%2e, optionally followed by %2f or %5c) or ..%2f ; or a known sensitive target /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, boot.ini or win.ini. Otherwise False.

title: Flag insecure code patterns
prompt:
DEFENSIVE static analysis (like a code scanner). Write `scan_code_vulns(code: str) -> list[str]` returning the sorted unique indicator names found in a snippet of Python source. Detect (case-insensitive where sensible):
- 'code_execution': a call eval( or exec(
- 'command_injection': os.system( , or subprocess with shell=True
- 'hardcoded_secret': an assignment of password/passwd/api_key/apikey/secret/token to a quoted string of length >= 3, or an AWS key matching AKIA followed by 16 upper-case letters or digits
- 'weak_hash': hashlib.md5( or hashlib.sha1( (or a bare md5(/sha1( call)
- 'insecure_deserialization': pickle.load( or pickle.loads( , yaml.load( without a Loader= argument, or marshal.loads(
- 'disabled_tls_verification': verify=False , or ssl._create_unverified_context
Return [] if none are present. This only FLAGS risky patterns for review.

title: Find missing security headers
prompt: DEFENSIVE check. Write `missing_security_headers(headers: dict) -> list[str]` given a response's HTTP headers (a dict of header-name -> value). Return the sorted list of recommended security headers that are ABSENT, matching names case-insensitively, from exactly: Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options. Return the canonical spellings just listed. [] means all are present.

title: Classify a web attack
prompt: DEFENSIVE classification for an intrusion-detection system. Write `classify_web_attack(value: str) -> str` returning which single attack class a request value best matches, checked in this priority order, first match wins: 'sqli' (a tautology ' or 1=1 / ' or '1'='1, union select, or a quote then -- comment); 'xss' (<script, javascript:, or an on...= event handler); 'path_traversal' (../ , ..\\ , or %2e%2e); 'command_injection' (a shell metacharacter ; | || && or backticks or $( immediately followed by a command word such as cat ls id whoami nc curl wget bash sh); 'ssrf' (a URL to 127.0.0.1, localhost, 169.254.169.254, 0.0.0.0, [::1], or a file:// or gopher:// scheme). If none match, return 'none'. Recognises only.
